proof_summary: Writing \(D\) for decimal digit sum and \(N=10^k-1\), induction on the decimal digits proves \(D(x)+D(N-x)=9k\) and \(D(5x)+D(5(N-x))=9k\); for the latter, the last-digit contribution \(g(r)=\lfloor r/2\rfloor+5(r\bmod 2)\) satisfies \(g(r)+g(9-r)=9\). Thus the digit-sum differences at \(x\) and \(N-x\) have opposite signs, so complementary terms pairwise cancel across the central interval, making the corresponding endpoint cumulative sums equal.
